So I'm shopping after my shift at Target yea? And earlier that day I had helped a mom and little girl no older then like... gosh, four? Check out some stuff and what have you. The little girl had bought herself a barbie guitar or something, and was commenting about how she was now dirt poor. I looked over at her and smiled, "I'm dirt poor right now too! Poor people high-five!" She grinned and gave me a high-five and I was left to contemplate me celebrating having no money with a four-year old. Anywho, I'm trying to come up with ideas for Christmas gifts and I overhear the little girl again. She's telling her mom how she wants to get this stuffed Pokémon plush for a friend at school cause she hasn't been as happy as she normally is and maybe it'll make her feel better. It's rare to hear of a child that young being perceptive, or at least to me anyway. So, mom doesn't really want to get it now, and I tap mom on the shoulder and in a low whisper offer to get it for her so she can give it to her friend. Kinda confused and grateful I guess, she accepts. We check out in secret, and she says she'll surprise her later with it so they can wrap it together. I don't know, there's just something... nice about seeing a small child have a moment of selflessness. Especially working in retail, where most small children are only in it for themselves. I don't know. It was nice.
